solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stoat essentially mesmerises quarry

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central pair of letters of the next word is kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this ten-letter word
a quarry is an open mine

explanation.surface: A stoat transfixes the rabbit it is hunting before the kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' looks like the hunted prey in the picture, but here it is a place where stone is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the name for a stoat, especially in its white winter coat.

clue.text: Paint porcelain food container

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a paint finish with a slight sheen
second meaning: very thin, delicate china
third meaning: the casing round something we eat at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate meanings of one word, strung together to read like a shopping list for a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a semi-matt paint finish, a thin translucent porcelain, and the brittle outer casing of a hen's egg.

clue.text: A false name cunningly conceals cleric's latest wrongdoing

indicators.note: what conceals something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other
doing something cunningly means arranging it craftily, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the latest is the one that comes at the very end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of cleric

explanation.surface: A churchman's latest misconduct is hidden behind a cleverly chosen alias.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of 'a false name' are rearranged and the cleric's last letter slips in just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Malfeasance is a legal term for wrongdoing, especially by someone holding public office.

clue.text: Elegantly simple trap ensnares head of acquisitions

indicators.note: to ensnare is to catch and hold, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of acquisitions

explanation.surface: A plain, uncomplicated snare catches the leading acquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can describe something tidy and pleasingly simple in design, a near synonym of elegantly plain.

clue.text: Unsolicited correspondence from Spooner's brother's lock-up?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner's name signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: a brother is a monk, a lock-up is a jail; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Tongue-twisted mail seems to come from a sibling's garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' suggests a sibling and 'lock-up' a garage, but here they mean a member of a religious order and a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is advertising material sent to people who never asked for it, so it is unsolicited post.

clue.text: Desperately posh fellow enters rally periodically

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so these pieces sit within the other
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters
U means upper-class
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: An upper-class man desperately joins a rally from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a crossword convention; U comes first, then GENT goes inside the alternate letters of rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgently and desperately are synonyms, both describing acting with pressing need.

clue.text: Cats patrolling promenade devoid of large birds

indicators.note: patrolling surrounds an area, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: kitties are cats

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a promenade is a walk
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Cats prowl along a seafront walk where no big birds remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large birds' reads as a phrase, but large only gives the letter removed from the walk; the definition is just 'birds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittiwakes are a kind of small gull that nest on sea cliffs.

clue.text: Current measure affected declining leader

indicators.note: declining a leader means turning down the first letter, so it goes

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: A gauge of the electric current is altered as the leading figure falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The amp, short for ampere, is the unit by which electric current is measured.

clue.text: List shed light on an actuary's conclusion

parts.note: lit means illuminated
taken as written

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of actuary

explanation.surface: An actuary's final figures throw light on a list of risks.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long, repetitive list, from the series of prayers recited in church.

clue.text: Seduce cleaning lady on Malta

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman
M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to seduce the woman who cleans, while on holiday in Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to win them over by attraction, close in sense to seducing them.

clue.text: Giant barbarian besieges city bordering Italy

indicators.note: an army besieging a place surrounds it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: the Goths were a barbarian people

indicators.note: a border runs round the outside, so the city's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A huge barbarian lays siege to a town near the Italian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordering' suggests a neighbouring country; here the city's two letters sit either side of Italy's code, and the barbarian surrounds that.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant Philistine slain by David, and his name is used for any giant.

clue.text: Drug of choice for degenerate

parts.note: a go-to option is the one of choice
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: A favourite narcotic for someone who has gone to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse of their clue order: the drug 'of choice' is a go-to pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom meaning to deteriorate, the verb sense of degenerate.

clue.text: Report that chap would listen to

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: that chap is he; he would contracts

explanation.surface: That man would pay attention to a report.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to pay attention to it, a synonym of listening to advice.

clue.text: Mendicant caught in dodgy S African quarter

indicators.note: caught joins the mix, sitting in among the other letters being reworked
something dodgy is unreliable or shaky, so the letters will not stay in place

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written
north is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A beggar is nabbed in a shady district of a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' suggests a city district, but here it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Franciscan friars belong to a mendicant order, living on alms rather than owning property.

clue.text: Dim, heartless sycophant broadcast a slur about copper

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: a creep is a toady

indicators.note: about means around, so the scattered letters go round the metal
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A slow-witted, spineless toady spreads an insult about a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like slang for a police officer, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepuscular means relating to twilight, so dim or shadowy.

clue.text: Carefree island-dweller of old devoured by terrible sea turtle

indicators.note: what is devoured ends up inside the eater, so one piece is swallowed by the other
something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
O is a dictionary abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A happy-go-lucky islander of ancient times is eaten by a fearsome turtle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of old' reads as part of the definition, but 'of' is the link and 'old' is the letter swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters lived on an island, eating the lotus and drifting in dreamy indolence.

clue.text: Life initially is good in French city

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
taken as written
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: From the outset, life is pleasant in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' wants to go together, but French belongs with good; the definition is just 'city', and Lisbon is in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: One who's departing on Charlie's chopper

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a leaver is someone leaving

explanation.surface: Someone leaving rides on Charlie's helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but it is a butcher's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed knife used for chopping meat.

clue.text: Study about breaking First Nation's trust

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nation people of Canada
a den is a study or private room
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Research that breaches an Indigenous nation's confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Nation' is the Canadian term for an Indigenous people, here the Cree.
explanation.definitionFit: Credence means belief or trust, as in giving credence to a story.

clue.text: American bully left lunatic morsel of food

parts.note: to haze is US slang for bullying new recruits
L is the abbreviation for left
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A US thug abandoned a crazed scrap of food.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage, hazing is the bullying initiation of newcomers, as at colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut is a small edible nut, a bite-sized piece to eat.

clue.text: Question popular vocalists on the radio

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: what comes over the radio is only heard, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a choir is a body of singers

explanation.surface: Interrogate chart-topping singers being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask, the verb sense of question.

clue.text: Jellyfish from sea west of America

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is the left-hand side, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the USA

explanation.surface: A jellyfish drifting in from the ocean off the American coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the zoological term for the free-swimming, bell-shaped form of a jellyfish.

clue.text: Raises highly topical issue

parts.note: ups is a verb meaning raises
a hot topic is one of great current interest

explanation.surface: Someone brings up a pressing current-affairs matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a topic for debate, but here it means result.
explanation.definitionFit: Upshot means the final outcome, and issue can mean the result that something leads to.

clue.text: Bishop ridicules vainglorious claims

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rag is to tease or mock

explanation.surface: A churchman mocks someone's boastful assertions.
explanation.definitionFit: Brags, as a plural noun, are boastful statements made out of vanity.

clue.text: Print media mostly filled with youthful wannabees

indicators.note: a thing filled with something holds it inside
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the press is newspapers
tender years are young years

explanation.surface: Newspapers stuffed with young hopefuls eager for fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretenders lay claim to a status, like a throne, they do not have, much as aspirants do.

clue.text: Extract of lilac heals pain

indicators.note: an extract is a portion taken from inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy distilled from lilac relieves pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' suggests a herbal essence, and that picture is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Setter repeated idea that's doing the rounds

indicators.note: repeated means said twice, so the same piece appears two times in a row

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the same piece again

explanation.surface: The compiler keeps restating a fashionable notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a concept or joke passed from person to person, typically spreading online.

clue.text: Catch nurse neglecting daughter's comfort

parts.note: to catch what is said is to hear it

indicators.note: neglecting something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A sick child's carer is caught failing to look after her.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them, and comfort as a verb means to cheer or console.

clue.text: Times article sent up East 17

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up reads it from the bottom, so it is backwards

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign
a is the indefinite article
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A newspaper story mocks the boy band East 17.
explanation.walkthrough: East 17 was a 1990s pop group, but East is wordplay and 17 refers to the answer at 17-across, a chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe is a chopping tool, so it shares the sense of the cleaver at 17.

clue.text: Garden mole isn't regularly seen? Mischievous creature!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Is a mole in the garden not often spotted? What a rascal!
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for unexplained mechanical faults.

clue.text: Conservatives defending extremely hardline ideas

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Tories are UK Conservatives

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tories stand up for uncompromising policies.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories is the everyday name for members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are systems of thought proposed to explain something, a type of idea.

clue.text: Lament taking part of sinister German revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
taking part of means using only a portion, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Mourning the role played by a menacing German insurgent.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorrow over it, a synonym of lamenting it.
